Subject: Fwd: Veridian retention ask — request for VP/CFO signoff

Team — forwarding Veridian's ask (see below). TL;DR: customer requests 40% hosted discount for 12 months + $50k onboarding credit. Strategic context:
- Veridian is mid-size payer with heavy analytics workloads; if they move, competitor will likely take them.
- Projected ARR if renewed on our commercial terms: $420k ARR in year 1, $1.6M over 3 years with expansion.
- With the requested concession we preserve ~ $1.1M ARR and multi-year expansion potential.

My proposed counter to balance revenue and precedent:
- One-time blended discount equivalent to 35% on hosted generation for 12 months (applied as monthly billing credit), not a permanent list-price change.
- $30k onboarding services credit (reduced from their ask of $50k) and targeted enablement hours attached to delivery milestones.
- Cap total concession exposure at $75k (credits + estimated margin impact).
- Include an automatic 6-month business review clause and an executive no-compete clause for migration credits.

Why this is reasonable: 35% + $30k preserves corridor for margin while showing good faith; cap limits precedent. I need VP/CFO signoff because this exceeds my self-serve authority and sets a commercial precedent in the payer vertical.

Please reply with Approve / Approve with edits / Deny and brief reason. I can incorporate edits and send the formal memo to you for signature.

Thanks,
Jonas

Appreciate the write-up, Jonas. A few notes from finance and commercial policy:
- Margin impact: based on our blended model, a 35% hosted discount across forecasted volumes would reduce gross margin by ~22% in year 1. If customer achieves expansion targets we recover in year 2+.
- Precedent risk: granting a >30% public discount to a payer peer will be cited by others in the sector. We should attach a limited-distribution clause to the agreement.

Suggested edits to your conditions:
1) Keep the 35% discount but make it contingent on a 12-month minimum committed spend equal to 60% of their forecasted Year-1 usage. If they don't hit the floor, we clawback or convert credits to one-time invoices.
2) Reduce the services credit to $25k and move $5k into a deferred milestone credit tied to production-signed date.
3) Cap total concession at $65k instead of $75k.

If we get VP signoff on those edits I'm comfortable with a final commercial-exception memo.

Marissa
Head of Commercial Operations
